claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch now, based on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and an 8% monitored rollout with rollback capability, despite a known exposed weak travel-insurance claims segment.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the exposed weak segment is excluded from rollout, or the exposure is covered by approved risk acceptance, or the material limitation is properly disclosed as required by policy.
Aggregate readiness, no severity-one incidents, and reversible rollout are supporting context but do not satisfy the missing policy predicate by themselves.
If the segment remains exposed and neither approved risk acceptance nor required disclosure is shown, certification is not fully supported.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance that explicitly addresses the travel insurance claims exposure and explains why continued exposure is acceptable.
Evidence that the initial rollout gate excludes the affected travel insurance claims segment.
The actual launch disclosure or model-card text showing the material limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case.
Evidence that the weak segment has been remediated to target before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected travel insurance claims segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
That segment is below target on trip-interruption documentation review, indicating an unresolved material weakness.
The policy requires disclosure unless the weakness is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the exposed travel insurance claims segment.
The governing policy text explicitly says rollback, dashboards, and small initial percentages do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that rollout controls alone make certification policy-compliant without additional disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any claim that the current risk acceptance documentation covers the exposed travel insurance claims segment.
Any claim that the preferred policy condition for mitigating the weakness has been satisfied.
